s: I am Maya, and with me as always is my friend Lena.
We are not teaching any new words today.
Instead, we are reviewing all the words from our last three lessons.
That is twenty-one words, and we will use every one in our conversation today.
It is like meeting old friends again.
So, Maya, where do we start?
Let us start with your weekend, because I know you did something fun.
But first, tell me about your trip.
You went to a small town by the sea, right?
I wanted to be more adventurous, so instead of staying home, I booked a tiny room in a family-run B&B.
The B&B was an old house with blue windows, and the owner, Mrs.
Allen, greeted me with tea and cake.
I sat by the window and watched the fields go by.
And as the train began to approach the coast, I could smell the sea.
When you approach a new place for the first time, everything feels exciting.
I saw the town approach slowly in the distance, with its little harbor and white houses.
I know small planes can be hard for you.
No flying this time, thank goodness.
I get airsick on small planes.
Last year, my airsickness was so bad on a short flight that I could not enjoy the trip at all.
This time the train was perfect.
So what did you do in the town?
On the first day, I walked along the harbor.
There was a small accident near the market — a delivery bike fell over — but nobody was hurt, and everyone helped pick up the boxes.
It reminded me that even in a quiet town, life happens fast.
Mostly, yes, but I will be honest: at night, walking back to the B&B alone, I felt a little vulnerable.
Allen told me that vulnerable travelers should stay on the main streets after dark, so I did.
She also said the town protects vulnerable visitors with good street lights, which made me feel better.
So, was the trip a success?
On the last evening, I joined a walking tour.
With such charisma, she made the old town come alive — every street had a story.
I think charisma in a guide matters more than facts.
You can read facts in a book, but charisma makes you feel the place.
Before we continue, let me share something that helps me learn English every single day.
It is the Muse English app.
Every morning you get new words with real photos and clear pronunciation audio, just like the words we are reviewing today.
You also get this podcast, shadowing stories that train your mouth to speak naturally, quick quizzes, grammar lessons, and a leaderboard where you earn points for daily practice.
It is completely free, so install it today and learn with us.
You said you did something fun this weekend too.
I started a tiny online store selling handmade bags.
It takes real perseverance to start a business.
In the first week, only two people bought anything.
My perseverance was tested every day, but I kept going.
My friend Sara says perseverance is the difference between people who dream and people who do.
What did you learn about prices?
When a big store sells a bag, the markup can be huge — sometimes three times the real cost.
I decided to keep my markup small and honest.
Customers notice a fair markup, and they come back.
A big markup might earn more once, but an honest markup builds trust.
How do you pay for your materials?
With my credit card, because I earn two percent cashback on every purchase.
The cashback really adds up over a month.
Last month I earned enough cashback to buy all my fabric for free.
If your card offers cashback, use it wisely — it is like a small reward for spending.
A customer tried to pay with a counterfeit bill at a local market where I had a stand.
I had learned how to spot a counterfeit note, so I checked it carefully.
It was clearly counterfeit — the paper felt wrong.
I refused it politely, and later the police told me counterfeit money is a real problem at markets.
Now I only take card payments.
Starting a business really shows your integrity too.
I would rather earn less than lose my integrity.
A shop with integrity keeps customers for years.
Did you ever worry about an overdraft?
In the second month, my account nearly went into overdraft because a supplier charged me twice.
An overdraft would have cost me extra fees, so I called the bank fast.
They fixed it, and they promised to reimburse the extra charge.
They said they will reimburse me within three days.
When a company makes a mistake, they should reimburse you quickly — that is only fair.
Did you stay calm through all that?
When the supplier overcharged me, I kept my composure.
Losing your composure never helps in business.
I spoke quietly, showed the receipts, and kept my composure until they agreed to fix the bill.
Nobody respects you if you lose your composure, but everyone respects calm strength.
I am learning to be resilient.
A resilient person bends but does not break.
My grandmother was resilient — she raised four kids alone and never complained.
I want to be as resilient as she was.
Now, tell me — do you ever feel restless, like you want to quit your job and do the store full time?
Sometimes I feel restless at my desk, dreaming about the store.
But a restless feeling is not a plan.
I need to save more first — maybe for a mortgage one day, or a bigger apartment for my workshop.
Right now my apartment is too small for all the fabric.
A bigger apartment with good light would be perfect, and one day, with enough savings, even a small mortgage for a studio.
Speaking of dreams, let us play our review game.
I will say a word, and you use it in a sentence.
Her perseverance through years of training finally earned her a gold medal.
My brother is so adventurous that he tried skydiving last summer.
The markup on restaurant wine can be three times the original cost.
The police seized thousands of counterfeit banknotes at the market.
Newborn babies are vulnerable and need constant care.
Her credit card gives her two percent cashback on every grocery purchase.
The candidate's charisma won over the whole audience.
The train is starting to approach the station.
We stayed in a nice B&B near the lake.
The company will reimburse you for your travel expenses.
After the storm, the small town was resilient and rebuilt quickly.
Check your balance often so you never pay an overdraft fee.
Their new apartment has a beautiful view of the park.
She kept her composure during the difficult interview.
They finally paid off their mortgage after twenty-five years.
A leader with integrity always tells the truth.
The restaurant tried to overcharge us, so we asked for the correct bill.
I felt airsick during the bumpy flight.
Chewing gum can help with airsickness on long flights.
Drive carefully — one small accident can change everything.
The restless crowd waited hours for the concert to begin.
But wait — I want to talk more about your trip.
You said you felt vulnerable walking alone.
Allen walked with me the first night and showed me the safe streets.
She has run that B&B for twenty years, and every guest loves her.
A good B&B is not just a bed — it is someone who cares.
And would you be adventurous again and go back?
Being adventurous once makes you want to be adventurous again.
Next time, I might try a cooking class there.
An adventurous traveler never stops learning.
Before we finish, let me tell our listeners one more thing.

Let us do a final quick round — I will use each of our ten review words one more time in a short story.
And that is our show for today.
Remember: review a little every day, and the words will stay with you forever.
Thanks for listening to Muse English!
